--- title: "Module 1 - Tutorial 2" subtitle: "From Clean SEC Text to TF-IDF Features" number-sections: true date: "2026-02-01" date-modified: today date-format: long engine: jupyter format: html: code-overflow: wrap categories: ['SEC Text', 'TF-IDF', 'NLP Foundations', 'Language Probability', 'Guided Implementation', 'Evaluation'] description: "Guides students through a hands-on implementation of From Clean SEC Text to TF-IDF Features, with reusable code patterns, validation checks, and artifacts for later labs and assignments." execute: echo: true eval: true --- ## Module Learning Objectives {.unnumbered} By the end of Module 1, students should be able to: 1. preprocess SEC text consistently 2. build interpretable count-based feature representations 3. compare classical and neural-ready text pipelines 4. prepare reusable artifacts for assignment work ## Tutorial Learning Objectives {.unnumbered} By the end of this tutorial you will be able to: 1. Load a small SEC text sample for one or two companies. 2. Clean and tokenize text consistently. 3. Build a vocabulary and simple document-term counts. 4. Convert those counts into TF-IDF features. 5. Interpret top words before moving to the full Assignment 1 workflow. ## Recommended Dataset {.unnumbered} Use one of the following: - a small sample of SEC 10-K text for a single company - a few files from `data/SEC-10K-2024` - a few extracted sections from Item 1A or Item 7 The goal is to learn the workflow on a small scale before the full assignment corpus. ## How This Tutorial Connects {.unnumbered} - `M01_Lab1` focuses on preprocessing discipline and text inspection. - `M01_Lab2` introduces representation learning and embeddings. - `M01_A` expects students to build reusable SEC text features at larger scale. - Module 1 participation work can use the same cleaned text and vocabulary logic. ## Setup {.unnumbered} ::: {#80395aac .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path from collections import Counter import re import pandas as pd from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer ``` ::: ## Step 1: Load a Small SEC Sample {.unnumbered} ::: {#3d786486 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sample_dir = Path("../data/SEC-10K-2024") txt_files = sorted(sample_dir.glob("*.txt"))[:3] docs = [] for f in txt_files: text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") docs.append({"source": f.stem, "text": text[:12000]}) sample_df = pd.DataFrame(docs) sample_df.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Step 2: Clean the Text {.unnumbered} ::: {#9321279d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} def clean_text(text: str) -> str: text = text.lower() text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\\s]", " ", text) text = re.sub(r"\\s+", " ", text).strip() return text sample_df["clean_text"] = sample_df["text"].apply(clean_text) sample_df[["source", "clean_text"]].head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Step 3: Build a Simple Vocabulary View {.unnumbered} ::: {#5d5fa30c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} all_tokens = " ".join(sample_df["clean_text"]).split() token_counts = Counter(all_tokens) pd.DataFrame(token_counts.most_common(20), columns=["token", "count"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
